He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball|Northern Illinois Huskies]] and the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]] before being drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 58th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. Nader has also played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He is one of two Egyptian-born players to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), the other being [[Alaa Abdelnaby]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Alexandria]], Egypt, Nader started his career at [[Maine East High School]], before transferring to [[Niles North High School|Niles North]].{{cite web |last1=Martorano |first1=Dion |title=Maine East Alum Competing In NBA Finals |url=https://www.journal-topics.com/articles/maine-east-alum-competing-in-nba-finals/ |website=Journal & Topics |access-date=May 25, 2023 |date=July 14, 2021}} He averaged 23.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game as a senior at Niles North and led the [[Niles North High School|Vikings]] to a 24–6 record and their first sectional championship and [[Central Suburban League]] titles in the school's 47-year history. He garnered First Team All-State honors from the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'',{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Helfgot|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/highschool/ct-spt-0403-prep-bkb-all-state-first-20110402-htmlstory.html |title=Boys basketball: 2011 Chicago Tribune All-State first team: Two All-Americans, two Mr. Basketballs and a Nader make up top five |work=ChicagoTribune.com |date=April 2, 2011 |access-date=June 25, 2015}} earned ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' Class 4A Second Team All-State recognition, and named to the [[ESPN]] Chicago All-Area team.{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Powers|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/994/boys-basketball-all-area-team-2009-10 |title=Boys basketball all-area team 2010-11 |work=ESPN.com |date=March 17, 2011 |access-date=June 25, 2015}} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Nader enrolled at [[Northern Illinois University]] and appeared in all 31 games starting in 29 of them. He averaged a team-best 10.4 points, third among [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] freshmen; and 4.2 rebounds, second-best among [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] freshmen. Nader recorded 21 steals and a team-high 22 blocked shots, the best among conference freshmen. He made his first collegiate start in the season opener at [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], scoring nine points and grabbing four rebounds. He scored in double figures in 17 games, including three games of 20-plus points as well as having a season-best 26 points against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]]. Nader's freshman season earned him [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |url=http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030712aab.html |title=Nader Named to MAC All-Freshman Team |work=NIUHuskies.com |date=March 7, 2012 |access-date=June 25, 2015 |archive-date=June 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626113324/http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030712aab.html |url-status=dead }} ===Sophomore season=== Nader began the season as a preseason All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] West selection. He started 18 of the 19 games he played in, leading the team in scoring at 13.1 points while averaging 5.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and shooting 77.2 percent from the free-throw line (44-57 FT). He scored in double figures 13 times, including three games with 20-plus points. Abdel posted 23 points on 4-of-5 shooting from 3-point range against [[Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball|Central Michigan]] (8-12 FG). He was named [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] West Player of the Week on Feb 4 after averaging 22.5 points and 11.0 rebounds during the week.{{cite web |url=http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020413aaa.html |title=Nader Named MAC West Player of the Week |work=NIUHuskies.com |date=February 4, 2013 |access-date=June 25, 2015 |archive-date=June 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626101219/http://www.niuhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/020413aaa.html |url-status=dead }} In spite of Nader's contributions, the Huskies finished last in the MAC West division and had a 5–15 team record overall, and it was reported that he would be transferring to another school.{{cite web|first=Raphielle|last=Johnson|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/28/report-northern-illinois-leading-scorer-abdel-nader-to-transfer/ |title=Report: Northern Illinois leading scorer Abdel Nader to transfer |work=NBCSports.com |date=March 28, 2013 |access-date=June 25, 2015}} ===Junior season=== Nader eventually transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|first=Travis |last=Hines |url=http://amestrib.com/sections/sports/isu-cyclones/men%E2%80%99s-basketball-northern-illinois-transfer-nader-headed-isu.html |title=Men's Basketball: Northern Illinois transfer Nader headed to ISU |work=AmesTrib.com |date=April 26, 2013 |access-date=June 25, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626100423/http://amestrib.com/sections/sports/isu-cyclones/men%E2%80%99s-basketball-northern-illinois-transfer-nader-headed-isu.html |archive-date=June 26, 2015 }} He had to sit out the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–2014]] season, becoming eligible again for the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15]] season. Nader saw action in 32 games, averaging 5.8 points and 2.9 rebounds in 16.4 minutes per game. He was tied for second on the team with 16 blocked shots. He grabbed six boards, two blocks, two steals, and hit 6-of-10 field goals, including 4-of-6 behind the arc to score 19 points in [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State's]] victory at [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Leistikow |url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2014/12/12/cyhawk-showdown-adbel-nader-naz-long-aaron-white-carver-hawkeye-arena/20334251/ |title=Iowa State dismantles Hawkeyes in Cy-Hawk showdown |work=DesmoinesRegister.com |date=December 12, 2014 |access-date=June 25, 2015}} He matched his season-high with 19 points at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]]. Nader scored 11 points and had six rebounds at home against [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]. He scored seven consecutive points in a key second-half run against the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] and blocked a fastbreak layup with 2:48 left that would have given the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] the lead.{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Birch|url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2015/01/20/abdel-nader-iowa-state-basketball-cyclones-kansas-state-big-conference-hilton-coliseum/22087443/ |title=Abdel Nader's big block alters course of Iowa State's win |work=DesmoinesRegister.com |date=January 20, 2015 |access-date=June 25, 2015}} Nader averaged 11.2 points and 5.3 rebounds when playing at least 20 minutes, ISU was 8–1 in those games. ==Professional career== ===Maine Red Claws (2016–2017)=== On June 24, 2016, Nader was drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 58th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-2016-draft-results|title=Boston Celtics 2016 Draft Results|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}} He then joined the Celtics for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-announce-2016-summer-league-roster/|title=Celtics Announce 2016 Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=July 4, 2016}} On October 31, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|title=2016 Training Camp Roster Announced|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104004654/http://maine.dleague.nba.com/news/2016-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} On April 14, 2017, he was named the 2016–17 [[NBA Development League Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Development League Rookie of the Year]], becoming the first internationally born player to be named NBA D-League Rookie of the Year and the third Red Claws player to earn the honor. Nader averaged 21.3 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.9 assists in 40 games, propelling the Red Claws to a 29–21 record and the Eastern Conference's second seed in the 2017 NBA D-League Playoffs. In addition to shooting 44.6 percent from the floor, Nader recorded a team-high 99 three-pointers. He also tallied 16 points, four rebounds and four assists during the 2017 D-League All-Star Game in [[New Orleans]]. ===Boston Celtics (2017–2018)=== On July 14, 2017, Nader agreed to a 4-year, $6M deal with the Celtics.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/maine-red-claws-abdel-nader-named-nba-d-league-rookie-year/|title=Maine Red Claws' Abdel Nader Named NBA D-League Rookie of the Year|work=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2017|access-date=April 19, 2017|archive-date=June 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170612200945/http://dleague.nba.com/news/maine-red-claws-abdel-nader-named-nba-d-league-rookie-year/|url-status=dead}} He made his NBA debut on October 18 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400974703|title=Bucks vs. Celtics - Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=April 28, 2018}} During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the Maine Red Claws.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Maine-Red-Claws/5/Transaction-History/2018|title=2017-2018 Maine Red Claws Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 23, 2018}} In four games with the Red Claws, he averaged 21.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game. Nader posted 3.1 points and 1.4 rebounds per game with the Celtics, and appeared in 11 playoff games during Celtics Eastern Conference Finals run.{{cite news|title=Final 2017-18 NBA G League stats for ex-Iowa collegians|url=http://www.thegazette.com/final-nba-g-league-stats-for-ex-iowa-collegians-20180327|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=March 27, 2018}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018–2020)=== On July 23, 2018, Nader was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Rodney Purvis]]. Oklahoma City also received cash considerations in the deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/nader-180723|title=Thunder Acquires Abdel Nader|work=NBA.com|date=July 23, 2018|access-date=July 23, 2018}} On November 28, 2019, Nader scored his career-high 23 points with two rebounds in a 136–119 loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/239793/abdel-nader-goes-off-career-high-23-points.php|title=Abdel Nader goes off for career-high 23 points|date=November 28, 2019}} ===Phoenix Suns (2020–2022)=== On November 16, 2020, the Thunder traded Nader and [[Chris Paul]] to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]], [[Ricky Rubio]], [[Ty Jerome]], [[Jalen Lecque]], and a protected 2022 first-round pick.{{cite web|title=Suns complete trade for Chris Paul, Abdel Nader|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/features/suns-complete-trade-chris-paul-abdel-nader|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 16, 2020|date=November 16, 2020}} After getting a [[concussion]] in a December 2020 preseason against the [[Utah Jazz]],[https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-abdel-nader-in-concussion-protocol/ Suns' Abdel Nader: In concussion protocol] he made his season debut on January 11, 2021, against the [[Washington Wizards]].[https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-was-0022000152 Beal Pours In 34 As Wizards Cruise Past Suns (Beal scores 34, Wizards beat Suns 128-107 for first home win)] On January 28, Nader scored a season-high 16 points in a blowout 114–93 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Suns Pull Away From Warriors, Climb Above .500 (Suns snap 3-game skid, roll to 114-93 win over Warriors)|first=David|last=Brandt|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-phx-0022000286|website=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=January 29, 2021}} On March 4, he had a near-double-double performance with 14 points and a career-high 9 rebounds off the bench in another blowout victory over Golden State, this time ending with a 120–98 win.{{cite web|title=Payne big off bench as Suns dispatch Warriors (Suns cruise past short-handed Warriors 120-98)|first=David|last=Brandt|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-phx-0022000185|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2021|access-date=March 8, 2021}} Nader made the [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but the Suns lost in 6 games to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On August 6, 2021, Nader re-signed with the Suns.{{cite web|title=SUNS RE-SIGN ABDEL NADER|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-re-sign-abdel-nader|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2021|date=August 6, 2021}} Nader was then later waived on February 10, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3015431/phoenix-suns-waive-abdel-nader-release-justin-jackson/|website=arizonasports.com|title=Phoenix Suns waive Abdel Nader, release Justin Jackson|access-date=February 10, 2022|date=February 10, 2022}} ===S.E. Melbourne Phoenix (2023–2024)=== On December 12, 2023, Nader signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the rest of the [[2023–24 NBL season|2023–24 season]].{{cite web|title=Phoenix Sign Abdel Nader to Roster|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/phoenix-sign-abdel-nader-to-roster|website=SEMPhoenix.com.au|access-date=December 12, 2023|date=December 12, 2023}} == International career == Nader is eligible for the [[Egypt men's national basketball team|Egypt national team]] and has confirmed that he would be making his debut at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{Cite web |last=Soliman |first=Seif |date=2023-03-05 |title=Abdel Nader confirms World Cup participation with Egypt |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2023/03/05/abdel-nader-world-cup-egypt/ |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=KingFut |language=en-GB}} However, he managed to complete the procedures to represent Egypt in March 2024.{{cite web |last=Gaballah |first=Ali Ismail |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2024/03/03/abdel-nader-eligible-egypt-2/ |title=BASKETBALL: Abdel Nader eligible to represent Egypt |publisher=KingFut |date=3 March 2024 }} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
